explain: The symbols Mac uses for keys. Every shortcut here uses them.
Quick Open: type part of a file name and jump to it.
example: Open styles.css without using the mouse.

explain: Command Palette: search for any VS Code command by name.
Shows or hides the sidebar, to get more room for code.
Opens the Explorer (the list of files).
example: Find a file in the project.

explain: Saves the file.
Closes the open tab.
example: Close files you are done with.

explain: Switches between your open tabs.
example: Jump back to the file you were just in.

explain: Splits the editor, so you see two files side by side.
example: HTML on the left, CSS on the right.

explain: Opens or hides the terminal inside VS Code.
example: Run python3 main.py without leaving VS Code.

explain: Opens Settings.
Go to a line number.
example: An error says line 42: jump there.

explain: Go to a function or heading in this file by name.
Go to where a function or variable is defined.
example: Click a function name, press F12.

explain: Go back to where you were before.
Comments out the line (or the selected lines). Press again to undo it.
example: Turn off some code for a moment.

explain: Moves the line up or down.
example: Reorder lines without cut and paste.

explain: Copies the line below itself.
example: Make a second similar line quickly.

explain: Deletes the whole line.
example: Remove a line in one step.

explain: With nothing selected, cuts the whole line.
Starts a new line below (or above), even with the cursor in the middle of a line.
example: Add a line without going to the end first.

explain: Indents or un-indents the line.
Formats the whole file: fixes spaces and indentation.
Shows suggestions for what you can type here.
example: See what methods a list has.

explain: Quick Fix: shows fixes for the problem under the cursor.
example: A red squiggle: let VS Code fix it.

explain: Renames a variable or function everywhere it is used.
Turns word wrap on or off, so long lines fit the screen.
example: Read a long paragraph in HTML.

explain: Selects the word, then the next same word each time you press it. Type to change them all.
Selects every same word in the file.
Adds another cursor where you click. Type in many places at once.
example: Add the same class to three lines.

explain: Adds a cursor on the line below (or above).
example: Type at the start of five lines at once.

explain: Selects the whole line. Press again for the next line.
example: Select lines to move or delete.

explain: Grows the selection: word, then the string, then the whole block.
Finds text in this file.
Finds and replaces in this file.
Searches in every file of the project.
example: Where else did I use this class?

explain: In an .html file, type ! and press Tab (or Enter): you get the whole starting page (doctype, head, body).
example: The first thing you type in a new HTML file.

explain:
Tag with a class: becomes
. A bare .box makes a div too.
Tag with an id: becomes <section id="about"></section>.
> puts a tag inside another, *3 repeats it: a list with three items.
example: nav>a*4 for a menu with four links.

explain: + puts tags next to each other.
$ becomes a number: item1, item2, item3.
{ } puts text inside the tag.
[ ] sets attributes.
Fills in placeholder text. lorem10 gives ten words.
Makes <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">.
Makes <script src=""></script>.
( ) groups a piece so + continues after it.
example: A whole page layout in one line.

explain: In a .css file: margin: 10px;  and  padding: 10px 20px;
width: 100%;  and  height: 50px;  (p means percent).
display: flex;  justify-content: center;  align-items: center;
example: Center something in three short words.

explain: display: grid;
font-size: 16px;  and  font-weight: 700;
background-color: #fff;  and  color: #000;  (then change the colour).
In a .js file, type log and pick it from the list: console.log();
for makes a counting loop; forof makes for (const item of list).
Makes an if (or if...else) block with the brackets ready.
Makes a function with the name, ( ) and { } ready.
Makes a try { } catch (error) { } block.
After a snippet appears, Tab jumps to the next blank to fill in.
example: Fill in the loop name, then the list.

explain: Run this from ⌘⇧P to make your own snippets for any language (Python, C, C++...). VS Code has none built in for those; extensions can add some.
With the Python extension: runs the selected line(s) in a Python terminal.
example: Test one line without running the whole file.

explain: Spotlight: open any app or file by typing its name.
Switches between open apps.
Switches between windows of the same app.
Quits the app.
Screenshot of an area; ⌘⇧5 opens the screenshot and recording tool.
In Finder: shows or hides hidden files (like .gitignore).
Jumps to the start or end of the line.
example: Fix the start of a long line.

explain: Jumps one word left or right.
Deletes the word before the cursor; ⌘⌫ deletes to the start of the line.
Stops the program that is running.
Completes a file or folder name. Press twice to see the choices.
Goes through commands you typed before.
Searches your old commands. Type part of one, press Enter.
example: Find that long git command again.

explain: Jumps to the start or end of the command.
Deletes the whole command you are typing.
In Terminal.app: clears the screen.
example: A clean screen before a new task.

explain: Opens DevTools: see the HTML, CSS and errors of a page.
example: Find out why your page looks wrong.

explain: Opens the Console: see console.log output and errors.
Click any part of the page to see its HTML and CSS.
example: Which CSS makes this button blue?

explain: Reloads the page; ⌘⇧R reloads without the old saved copy.
example: Your CSS change does not show: ⌘⇧R.

explain: Jumps to the address bar.
Reopens the tab you just closed.
